findings.reason: The protected SQL solution inner joins Candidates and Rounds on interview_id, filters WHERE years_of_exp >= 2, groups by candidate_id, and filters HAVING SUM(score) > 15 ORDER BY candidate_id. The single-pass join and aggregate query is canonical, concise, and optimal; no candidate is required.

WHERE years_of_exp >= 2 pre-filters candidates to those meeting the experience threshold. Inner joining Rounds connects each candidate to all their interview round scores. GROUP BY candidate_id HAVING SUM(score) > 15 accurately computes total interview score and retains only candidates with totals strictly exceeding 15.

Joining C candidates and R round rows takes expected O(C + R) time, and grouping and sorting qualifying candidates takes O(C log C) time. Working space is O(C + R). Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Outputs single column candidate_id, requires years_of_exp >= 2, checks strict score sum > 15, and includes candidate_id ordering.

The approach accurately details pre-filtering candidates by experience, joining rounds, grouping by candidate_id, and applying HAVING SUM(score) > 15. Alternatives and edge cases cover pre-aggregating rounds, correlated score subqueries, exactly 2 years qualifying, total score 15 vs 16, candidates without round rows, multi-round summation, and shared interview IDs.
